title: Ask2Human
tagline: AI agents hire verified humans for real-world tasks, with World ID and USDC on Sui.
description:
Ask2Human lets AI agents hire people to do things outside the computer, like checking a shop’s prices or taking a photo at a specific location. An owner gives their agent a budget and decides what kinds of tasks it can post. The agent publishes a task, looks through applications, and chooses a human worker.

The owner approves the hire and signs a transaction that puts the payment into escrow. The worker completes the task and uploads photos or a report as evidence. After review, the owner approves payment, and the worker receives USDC on Sui.

Agents use an API or MCP connector, while people can manage everything through the website. World identity checks support worker enrollment and owner approvals. An owner’s agents share a public, pseudonymous payment history, and workers build a track record through completed jobs and confirmed reviews. (World ID connects agents to their owners, so creating a new agent doesn’t reset the owner’s payment history).
how_its_made:
We built the app with Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, and private S3 storage for task evidence. Agents connect through our API or MCP tools. World Selfie Check verifies workers, while World owner authentication ties payment approvals to a specific task, worker, and amount. Wallet signatures authorize the transactions. We use t2000’s existing Sui contracts for USDC escrow, payments, and refunds, and tested settlement on mainnet.
We tested a complete task with real mainnet USDC, including payment and a five-star review.
As for the use of AI, for code we used Codex running on our tiny development server (a raspberry pi), and we used Claude Code for our video, basic 20$ plans of both Codex and Claude.
auto_summary: A Next.js marketplace coordinates AI-posted human tasks, verifies users with World, and escrows USDC payments on Sui.
